newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bendigo sees lower yr pre-tax profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bendigo sees lower yr pre-tax profit.

text.p: Bendigo Bank Ltd said on Friday it expected a lower core pre-tax profit for the year to June 30, 1997, due to a delcine in revenue from home lending.

However, the regional bank said its annual profit after-tax should not be significantly different from a year ago, although there would be additional abnormal expenses to complete the restructuring of Monte Paschi's Australian subsidiary.
Bendigo Bank reported a net profit of A$12.81 million for the year to June 30, 1996, and an operating profit of A$22.1 million.

Chairman Richard Guy said in a letter to shareholders that revenue from home lending would decline in the current year and that intense competition and aggressive price-setting in the marketplace had reduced the profitability of housing finance.

"To protect our lending franchise, we have taken a conscious decision to price our loans competitively and to continue to provide our borrowers with the added value they have come to expect from Bendigo Bank," Guy said.
This meant the bank's net interest margin had been reduced by 70 to 80 basis points over the current year.
Guy said that in order to reduce its dependence on housing lending the bank continued to develop a more diversified business through expansion of the bank's business lending.
"While these measures will partially offset reductions in income from housing lending, we anticipate a reduction in core pre-tax profit for the full year.

"After tax profit should not be significantly different from last year, however we expect there will be additional abnormal expenses to complete the restructuring of Monte Paschi and the reshaping of the bank following the change in profitability in housing," Guy said.
